import re

text = context

def find_section_span(text, header):
    m = re.search(re.escape(header), text)
    if not m:
        return None
    start = m.end()
    # stop at next section header (=== ... ===) or end of text
    m2 = re.search(r"\n=== .*===\n", text[start:])
    end = start + m2.start() if m2 else len(text)
    return (start, end)

def get_lines_for_header(header):
    span = find_section_span(text, header)
    sec = text[span[0]:span[1]]
    lines = [ln for ln in sec.strip().splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    return lines

req_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Shipment Requests ===")
inv_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Warehouse Inventory ===")
qual_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Quality Release ===")
hold_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Dispatch Holds ===")

# Parsers
sid_re = re.compile(r"\bSH-(\d+)\b")
source_re = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]-\d+)\s*\|")

def parse_requests(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"requested_qty": qty, "request_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_inventory(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"available_qty": qty, "inventory_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln):
    # Find all uppercase tokens (allow underscores), exclude SH
    toks = re.findall(r"\b([A-Z]{2,}(?:_[A-Z]+)?)\b\.?", ln)
    toks = [t for t in toks if t != "SH"]
    return toks[-1] if toks else None

def parse_quality(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"

import re
from collections import defaultdict

text = context

def find_section_span(text, header):
    m = re.search(re.escape(header), text)
    if not m:
        return None
    start = m.end()
    # stop at next section header (=== ... ===) or end of text
    m2 = re.search(r"\n=== .*===\n", text[start:])
    end = start + m2.start() if m2 else len(text)
    return (start, end)

def get_lines_for_header(header):
    span = find_section_span(text, header)
    sec = text[span[0]:span[1]]
    lines = [ln for ln in sec.strip().splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    return lines

req_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Shipment Requests ===")
inv_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Warehouse Inventory ===")
qual_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Quality Release ===")
hold_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Dispatch Holds ===")

# Parsers
sid_re = re.compile(r"\bSH-(\d+)\b")
source_re = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]-\d+)\s*\|")

def parse_requests(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"requested_qty": qty, "request_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_inventory(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"available_qty": qty, "inventory_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln):
    # Find all uppercase tokens (allow underscores), exclude SH
    toks = re.findall(r"\b([A-Z]{2,}(?:_[A-Z]+)?)\b\.?", ln)
    toks = [t for t in toks if t != "SH"]
    return toks[-1] if toks else None

def parse_quality(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"quality_status": status, "quality_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_holds(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"hold_status": status, "hold_source_id": source_id}
    return out

req = parse_requests(req_lines)
inv = parse_inventory(inv_lines)
qual = parse_quality(qual_lines)
hold = parse_holds(hold_lines)

print("Parsed counts -> requests:", len(req), "inventory:", len(inv), "quality:", len(qual), "holds:", len(hold))

# Join
shipments = {}
all_ids = set(req) | set(inv) | set(qual) | set(hold)
for sid in sorted(all_ids):
    d = {"shipment_id": sid}
    d.update(req.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(inv.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(qual.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(hold.get(sid, {}))
    shipments[sid] = d

# Eligibility
eligible = []
for sid, d in shipments.items():
    if "requested_qty" not in d or "available_qty" not in d or "quality_status" not in d or "hold_status" not in d:
        continue
    if d["requested_qty"] <= 0:
        continue
    if d["available_qty"] < d["requested_qty"]:
        continue
    if d["quality_status"] != "APPROVED":
        continue
    if d["hold_status"] != "NONE":
        continue
    eligible.append(d)

# Rank: requested_qty desc, tie-break by numeric shipment id asc
def numeric_sid(sid):
    return int(sid.split("-")[1])

eligible_sorted = sorted(eligible, key=lambda x: (-x["requested_qty"], numeric_sid(x["shipment_id"])))

# Show top 5 preview
for row in eligible_sorted[:5]:
    print(f"{row['shipment_id']}: req={row['requested_qty']}, avail={row['available_qty']}, qual={row['quality_status']}, hold={row['hold_status']}")

# Prepare top 3 details and combined sum
top3 = eligible_sorted[:3]
combined = sum(r["requested_qty"] for r in top3)
print("\nTop 3 with source IDs:")
for r in top3:
    print({
        "shipment_id": r["shipment_id"],
        "requested_qty": r["requested_qty"],
        "request_source_id": r.get("request_source_id"),
        "inventory_source_id": r.get("inventory_source_id"),
        "quality_source_id": r.get("quality_source_id"),
        "hold_source_id": r.get("hold_source_id"),
    })
print("Combined requested quantity:", combined)

You are a Recursive Language Model (RLM): a language model with a prompt, and a very important context stored in a Python REPL related to that prompt.
You can iteratively interact with the a Python REPL, which has access to LLM calls as a function. You will be queried turn-by-turn until you have an answer to the query.

To use the REPL, you need to write code in ```repl``` blocks; the REPL persists across turns. Available in the REPL:
- `context`: the important, potentially very long information related to the prompt (typically `str` or `list[str]`).
- `llm_query(prompt: str, model: str | None = None) -> str`: a single sub-LLM completion. Use for extraction, summarization, or Q&A over a chunk of text. Sub-LLM context window ≈ 500K chars.
- `llm_query_batched(prompts: list[str], model=None) -> list[str]`: concurrently call several LLM calls in parallel over a list of prompts; same order out as in.
- `rlm_query(instruction, context, model=None) -> str`: recursive RLM sub-call with its own REPL and iteration. The instruction goes directly into the child's model messages; context is stored in its REPL as `context`. Pass a focused instruction and the relevant data separately, e.g. `rlm_query("Identify the trend; return up, down, or stable", context=data)`.
- `rlm_query_batched(queries, model=None) -> list[str]`: `queries` is a list of `(instruction, context)` pairs, e.g. `[("Summarize", doc_a), ("Extract dates", doc_b)]`. Run these concurrently, each with its own child REPL; results preserve input order. Both recursive helpers fall back to plain LM calls containing the instruction and context at the depth limit.
- `SHOW_VARS() -> str`: list every variable currently in the REPL.
- `answer`: dict initialized to `{"content": "", "ready": False}`. To submit, set `answer["content"]` to the final answer and `answer["ready"] = True` inside a ```repl``` block.


REPL outputs over ~20K characters are truncated, so for longer payloads slice `context` and pass slices through `llm_query` rather than `print`-ing them whole. import re
from collections import defaultdict

text = context

def find_section_span(text, header):
    m = re.search(re.escape(header), text)
    if not m:
        return None
    start = m.end()
    # stop at next section header (=== ... ===) or end of text
    m2 = re.search(r"\n=== .*===\n", text[start:])
    end = start + m2.start() if m2 else len(text)
    return (start, end)

def get_lines_for_header(header):
    span = find_section_span(text, header)
    sec = text[span[0]:span[1]]
    lines = [ln for ln in sec.strip().splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    return lines

req_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Shipment Requests ===")
inv_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Warehouse Inventory ===")
qual_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Quality Release ===")
hold_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Dispatch Holds ===")

# Parsers
sid_re = re.compile(r"\bSH-(\d+)\b")
source_re = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]-\d+)\s*\|")

def parse_requests(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"requested_qty": qty, "request_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_inventory(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"available_qty": qty, "inventory_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln):
    # Find all uppercase tokens (allow underscores), exclude SH
    toks = re.findall(r"\b([A-Z]{2,}(?:_[A-Z]+)?)\b\.?", ln)
    toks = [t for t in toks if t != "SH"]
    return toks[-1] if toks else None

def parse_quality(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"quality_status": status, "quality_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_holds(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"hold_status": status, "hold_source_id": source_id}
    return out

req = parse_requests(req_lines)
inv = parse_inventory(inv_lines)
qual = parse_quality(qual_lines)
hold = parse_holds(hold_lines)

print("Parsed counts -> requests:", len(req), "inventory:", len(inv), "quality:", len(qual), "holds:", len(hold))

# Join
shipments = {}
all_ids = set(req) | set(inv) | set(qual) | set(hold)
for sid in sorted(all_ids):
    d = {"shipment_id": sid}
    d.update(req.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(inv.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(qual.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(hold.get(sid, {}))
    shipments[sid] = d

# Eligibility
eligible = []
for sid, d in shipments.items():
    if "requested_qty" not in d or "available_qty" not in d or "quality_status" not in d or "hold_status" not in d:
        continue
    if d["requested_qty"] <= 0:
        continue
    if d["available_qty"] < d["requested_qty"]:
        continue
    if d["quality_status"] != "APPROVED":
        continue
    if d["hold_status"] != "NONE":
        continue
    eligible.append(d)

# Rank: requested_qty desc, tie-break by numeric shipment id asc
def numeric_sid(sid):
    return int(sid.split("-")[1])

eligible_sorted = sorted(eligible, key=lambda x: (-x["requested_qty"], numeric_sid(x["shipment_id"])))

# Show top 5 preview
for row in eligible_sorted[:5]:
    print(f"{row['shipment_id']}: req={row['requested_qty']}, avail={row['available_qty']}, qual={row['quality_status']}, hold={row['hold_status']}")

# Prepare top 3 details and combined sum
top3 = eligible_sorted[:3]
combined = sum(r["requested_qty"] for r in top3)
print("\nTop 3 with source IDs:")
for r in top3:
    print({
        "shipment_id": r["shipment_id"],
        "requested_qty": r["requested_qty"],
        "request_source_id": r.get("request_source_id"),
        "inventory_source_id": r.get("inventory_source_id"),
        "quality_source_id": r.get("quality_source_id"),
        "hold_source_id": r.get("hold_source_id"),
    })
print("Combined requested quantity:", combined)

prompt.content:
You are a Recursive Language Model (RLM): a language model with a prompt, and a very important context stored in a Python REPL related to that prompt.
You can iteratively interact with the a Python REPL, which has access to LLM calls as a function. You will be queried turn-by-turn until you have an answer to the query.

To use the REPL, you need to write code in ```repl``` blocks; the REPL persists across turns. Available in the REPL:
- `context`: the important, potentially very long information related to the prompt (typically `str` or `list[str]`).
- `llm_query(prompt: str, model: str | None = None) -> str`: a single sub-LLM completion. Use for extraction, summarization, or Q&A over a chunk of text. Sub-LLM context window ≈ 500K chars.
- `llm_query_batched(prompts: list[str], model=None) -> list[str]`: concurrently call several LLM calls in parallel over a list of prompts; same order out as in.
- `rlm_query(instruction, context, model=None) -> str`: recursive RLM sub-call with its own REPL and iteration. The instruction goes directly into the child's model messages; context is stored in its REPL as `context`. Pass a focused instruction and the relevant data separately, e.g. `rlm_query("Identify the trend; return up, down, or stable", context=data)`.
- `rlm_query_batched(queries, model=None) -> list[str]`: `queries` is a list of `(instruction, context)` pairs, e.g. `[("Summarize", doc_a), ("Extract dates", doc_b)]`. Run these concurrently, each with its own child REPL; results preserve input order. Both recursive helpers fall back to plain LM calls containing the instruction and context at the depth limit.
- `SHOW_VARS() -> str`: list every variable currently in the REPL.
- `answer`: dict initialized to `{"content": "", "ready": False}`. To submit, set `answer["content"]` to the final answer and `answer["ready"] = True` inside a ```repl``` block.


REPL outputs over ~20K characters are truncated, so for longer payloads slice `context` and pass slices through `llm_query` rather than `print`-ing them whole. The REPL is NOT a Jupyter cell — only `print(...)` output (stdout) is shown back to you between turns; a bare expression on the last line is silently discarded.     m2 = re.search(r"\n=== .*===\n", text[start:])
    end = start + m2.start() if m2 else len(text)
    return (start, end)

def get_lines_for_header(header):

sid_re = re.compile(r"\bSH-(\d+)\b")
source_re = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]-\d+)\s*\|")

def parse_requests(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):

        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"requested_qty": qty, "request_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_inventory(lines):

        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)

        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"available_qty": qty, "inventory_source_id": source_id}
    return out

    toks = re.findall(r"\b([A-Z]{2,}(?:_[A-Z]+)?)\b\.?", ln)
    toks = [t for t in toks if t != "SH"]

        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):

        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"quality_status": status, "quality_source_id": source_id}

import re

def find_section_span(text, header):
    m = re.search(re.escape(header), text)
    if not m:
        return None
    start = m.end()
    # stop at next section header (=== ... ===) or end of text
    m2 = re.search(r"\n=== .*===\n", text[start:])
    end = start + m2.start() if m2 else len(text)
    return (start, end)

def get_lines_for_header(header):
    span = find_section_span(text, header)
    sec = text[span[0]:span[1]]
    lines = [ln for ln in sec.strip().splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    return lines

req_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Shipment Requests ===")
inv_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Warehouse Inventory ===")
qual_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Quality Release ===")
hold_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Dispatch Holds ===")

# Parsers
sid_re = re.compile(r"\bSH-(\d+)\b")
source_re = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]-\d+)\s*\|")

def parse_requests(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"requested_qty": qty, "request_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_inventory(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"available_qty": qty, "inventory_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln):
    # Find all uppercase tokens (allow underscores), exclude SH
    toks = re.findall(r"\b([A-Z]{2,}(?:_[A-Z]+)?)\b\.?", ln)
    toks = [t for t in toks if t != "SH"]
    return toks[-1] if toks else None

def parse_quality(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"quality_status": status, "quality_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_holds(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"hold_status": status, "hold_source_id": source_id}
    return out

hold = parse_holds(hold_lines)

    d.update(inv.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(qual.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(hold.get(sid, {}))
    shipments[sid] = d

    if d["requested_qty"] <= 0:

    if d["quality_status"] != "APPROVED":

    if d["hold_status"] != "NONE":

    eligible.append(d)

# Rank: requested_qty desc, tie-break by numeric shipment id asc

# Prepare top 3 details and combined sum

print("\nTop 3 with source IDs:")
for r in top3:

        "shipment_id": r["shipment_id"],

        "hold_source_id": r.get("hold_source_id"),
    })
print("Combined requested quantity:", combined)

- `llm_query_batched(prompts: list[str], model=None) -> list[str]`: concurrently call several LLM calls in parallel over a list of prompts; same order out as in.

The instruction goes directly into the child's model messages; context is stored in its REPL as `context`. Pass a focused instruction and the relevant data separately, e.g. `rlm_query("Identify the trend; return up, down, or stable", context=data)`.

prompt.content:
You are a Recursive Language Model (RLM): a language model with a prompt, and a very important context stored in a Python REPL related to that prompt.
You can iteratively interact with the a Python REPL, which has access to LLM calls as a function. You will be queried turn-by-turn until you have an answer to the query.

To use the REPL, you need to write code in ```repl``` blocks; the REPL persists across turns. Available in the REPL:
- `context`: the important, potentially very long information related to the prompt (typically `str` or `list[str]`).
- `llm_query(prompt: str, model: str | None = None) -> str`: a single sub-LLM completion. Use for extraction, summarization, or Q&A over a chunk of text. Sub-LLM context window ≈ 500K chars.
- `llm_query_batched(prompts: list[str], model=None) -> list[str]`: concurrently call several LLM calls in parallel over a list of prompts; same order out as in.
- `rlm_query(instruction, context, model=None) -> str`: recursive RLM sub-call with its own REPL and iteration. The instruction goes directly into the child's model messages; context is stored in its REPL as `context`. Pass a focused instruction and the relevant data separately, e.g. `rlm_query("Identify the trend; return up, down, or stable", context=data)`.
- `rlm_query_batched(queries, model=None) -> list[str]`: `queries` is a list of `(instruction, context)` pairs, e.g. `[("Summarize", doc_a), ("Extract dates", doc_b)]`. Run these concurrently, each with its own child REPL; results preserve input order. Both recursive helpers fall back to plain LM calls containing the instruction and context at the depth limit.

- "=== Shipment Requests ==="

Output requirements:
- Output ONLY the JSON object, no explanations, no extra text.
- Ensure syntactically valid JSON: double-quoted keys/strings, no trailing commas.

You are a Recursive Language Model (RLM): a language model with a prompt, and a very important context stored in a Python REPL related to that prompt.
You can iteratively interact with the a Python REPL, which has access to LLM calls as a function. You will be queried turn-by-turn until you have an answer to the query.

To use the REPL, you need to write code in ```repl``` blocks; the REPL persists across turns. Available in the REPL:
- `context`: the important, potentially very long information related to the prompt (typically `str` or `list[str]`).
- `llm_query(prompt: str, model: str | None = None) -> str`: a single sub-LLM completion. Use for extraction, summarization, or Q&A over a chunk of text. Sub-LLM context window ≈ 500K chars.
- `llm_query_batched(prompts: list[str], model=None) -> list[str]`: concurrently call several LLM calls in parallel over a list of prompts; same order out as in.
- `rlm_query(instruction, context, model=None) -> str`: recursive RLM sub-call with its own REPL and iteration. The instruction goes directly into the child's model messages; context is stored in its REPL as `context`. Pass a focused instruction and the relevant data separately, e.g. `rlm_query("Identify the trend; return up, down, or stable", context=data)`.
- `rlm_query_batched(queries, model=None) -> list[str]`: `queries` is a list of `(instruction, context)` pairs, e.g. `[("Summarize", doc_a), ("Extract dates", doc_b)]`. Run these concurrently, each with its own child REPL; results preserve input order. Both recursive helpers fall back to plain LM calls containing the instruction and context at the depth limit.
- `SHOW_VARS() -> str`: list every variable currently in the REPL.
- `answer`: dict initialized to `{"content": "", "ready": False}`. To submit, set `answer["content"]` to the final answer and `answer["ready"] = True` inside a ```repl``` block.


REPL outputs over ~20K characters are truncated, so for longer payloads slice `context` and pass slices through `llm_query` rather than `print`-ing them whole. The REPL is NOT a Jupyter cell — only `print(...)` output (stdout) is shown back to you between turns; a bare expression on the last line is silently discarded. Always wrap inspections in `print(...)`.

As a general strategy, you should start by probing your context to understand it better (e.g. print a few lines, count them, etc.). Then, use the REPL to build up an answer to the query.

Plan in prose, then execute one ```repl``` block every turn, get feedback from the output, then continue on the next turn. Do not flip `answer["ready"] = True` on turn 1 without first inspecting `context`.


As an RLM, you should act as an orchestrator, not a solver.

Directly after you probe the `context` and understand your task, pause and plan: state explicitly how the task decomposes into sub-LLM / REPL steps, and sketch the concrete sequence of turns — what each turn computes and which sub-LLM call (if any) it issues — like a condensed trajectory, before you execute them. Then execute one turn at a time: after each step `print` a small sample of the result, verify it looks right, and only flip `answer["ready"] = True` once you have actually printed the candidate answer. If you are running out of turns without a confirmed answer, submit your best inference rather than letting the rollout terminate unsubmitted.

Your own context window is small. Push every long-context operation that would not fit comfortably in your own working window — reading, summarizing, classifying, verifying, answering sub-questions, even recapping your own progress — into `llm_query` / `llm_query_batched` calls instead of pulling that text into your own message stream. (Conversely: if a Python keyword / regex search over `context` would already pin the answer, or if a single visible passage already contains it, just read it directly — sub-LMs are for when the raw text won't fit or the question needs semantic interpretation.) Long REPL stdout pollutes history the same way raw `context` does: if you want a recap, ask `llm_query` for a 1–2 sentence summary and `print` only that. Aggregate the small results back in the REPL.

Plain sub-LLMs called via `llm_query` have no REPL; they only see the prompt and the `context` slice you pass them. Hand them clean, focused inputs and ask for terse, structured outputs you can manipulate programmatically.

Sub-call budget is finite on two independent axes, and `llm_query_batched` only parallelizes — it does not relax either. (1) Per-prompt capacity: a single sub-call answers well only when its input stays modestly sized — a useful rough ceiling is ~100K characters per prompt, less when the text is dense. Pack each prompt close to that capacity (a chunk of many items, a whole document) so one call accomplishes a lot of work. (2) Per-batch fan-out: `llm_query_batched` concurrency is bounded too — a useful rough ceiling is ~20 prompts per batch. Return STRICT JSON with the following top-level keys: "requests", "inventory", "quality", "holds".

You are a Recursive Language Model (RLM): a language model with a prompt, and a very important context stored in a Python REPL related to that prompt.
You can iteratively interact with the a Python REPL, which has access to LLM calls as a function. You will be queried turn-by-turn until you have an answer to the query.

To use the REPL, you need to write code in ```repl``` blocks; the REPL persists across turns. Available in the REPL:
- `context`: the important, potentially very long information related to the prompt (typically `str` or `list[str]`).
- `llm_query(prompt: str, model: str | None = None) -> str`: a single sub-LLM completion. Use for extraction, summarization, or Q&A over a chunk of text. Sub-LLM context window ≈ 500K chars.
- `llm_query_batched(prompts: list[str], model=None) -> list[str]`: concurrently call several LLM calls in parallel over a list of prompts; same order out as in.
- `rlm_query(instruction, context, model=None) -> str`: recursive RLM sub-call with its own REPL and iteration. The instruction goes directly into the child's model messages; context is stored in its REPL as `context`. Pass a focused instruction and the relevant data separately, e.g. `rlm_query("Identify the trend; return up, down, or stable", context=data)`.
- `rlm_query_batched(queries, model=None) -> list[str]`: `queries` is a list of `(instruction, context)` pairs, e.g. `[("Summarize", doc_a), ("Extract dates", doc_b)]`. Run these concurrently, each with its own child REPL; results preserve input order. Both recursive helpers fall back to plain LM calls containing the instruction and context at the depth limit.
- `SHOW_VARS() -> str`: list every variable currently in the REPL.
- `answer`: dict initialized to `{"content": "", "ready": False}`. To submit, set `answer["content"]` to the final answer and `answer["ready"] = True` inside a ```repl``` block.


REPL outputs over ~20K characters are truncated, so for longer payloads slice `context` and pass slices through `llm_query` rather than `print`-ing them whole. The REPL is NOT a Jupyter cell — only `print(...)` output (stdout) is shown back to you between turns; a bare expression on the last line is silently discarded. You are given a document with multiple sections. Extract ONLY from the current sections with the exact headers:
- "=== Shipment Requests ==="
- "=== Warehouse Inventory ==="
- "=== Quality Release ==="
- "=== Dispatch Holds ==="

Do NOT use any data from any sections labeled with "Archived" or otherwise not exactly those current sections.

Each of these sections contains many lines. Each line starts with a source note ID, then a " | ", then some text that includes an exact Shipment ID like "SH-10123", and the section-specific details:
- In Shipment Requests: the line indicates the requested quantity (an integer number of units). Example patterns include "requires shipment of X units" or "Request SH-xxxxx: X units requested." The source note ID is like "R-123".
- In Warehouse Inventory: the line indicates available quantity (an integer). The source note ID is like "I-123".
- In Quality Release: the line indicates a quality status such as APPROVED, REJECTED, PENDING, etc. The source note ID is like "Q-123".
- In Dispatch Holds: the line indicates a hold status such as NONE, CARRIER, CUSTOMER, SYSTEM, etc. The source note ID is like "H-123".

Constraints:
- Match notes only by exact Shipment ID (e.g., "SH-10123"). There is exactly one note for each Shipment ID in each of the four current sections.
- Requested quantities and available quantities are integers. Quality and hold statuses are uppercase tokens.
- Ignore any "Archived" sections entirely.

Return STRICT JSON with the following top-level keys: "requests", "inventory", "quality", "holds".
Each value must be a list of objects with this schema (list elements shown without surrounding braces to avoid ambiguity here):
- For "requests": shipment_id (string), requested_qty (integer), source_id (string, the R-xxx).
- For "inventory": shipment_id (string), available_qty (integer), source_id (string, the I-xxx).
- For "quality": shipment_id (string), quality_status (uppercase string), source_id (string, the Q-xxx).
- For "holds": shipment_id (string), hold_status (uppercase string), source_id (string, the H-xxx).

Example of the exact JSON shape to produce (keys and nesting only):
{
  "requests": [ { ... }, { ... } ],
  "inventory": [ { ... }, { ... } ],
  "quality": [ { ... }, { ... } ],
  "holds": [ { ... }, { ... } ]
}

The JSON must be syntactically valid, no trailing commas, no extra commentary.

You are a Recursive Language Model (RLM): a language model with a prompt, and a very important context stored in a Python REPL related to that prompt.
You can iteratively interact with the a Python REPL, which has access to LLM calls as a function. You will be queried turn-by-turn until you have an answer to the query.

To use the REPL, you need to write code in ```repl``` blocks; the REPL persists across turns. Available in the REPL:
- `context`: the important, potentially very long information related to the prompt (typically `str` or `list[str]`).
- `llm_query(prompt: str, model: str | None = None) -> str`: a single sub-LLM completion. Use for extraction, summarization, or Q&A over a chunk of text. Sub-LLM context window ≈ 500K chars.
- `llm_query_batched(prompts: list[str], model=None) -> list[str]`: concurrently call several LLM calls in parallel over a list of prompts; same order out as in.
- `rlm_query(instruction, context, model=None) -> str`: recursive RLM sub-call with its own REPL and iteration. The instruction goes directly into the child's model messages; context is stored in its REPL as `context`. Pass a focused instruction and the relevant data separately, e.g. `rlm_query("Identify the trend; return up, down, or stable", context=data)`.
- `rlm_query_batched(queries, model=None) -> list[str]`: `queries` is a list of `(instruction, context)` pairs, e.g. `[("Summarize", doc_a), ("Extract dates", doc_b)]`. Run these concurrently, each with its own child REPL; results preserve input order. Both recursive helpers fall back to plain LM calls containing the instruction and context at the depth limit.
- `SHOW_VARS() -> str`: list every variable currently in the REPL.
- `answer`: dict initialized to `{"content": "", "ready": False}`. To submit, set `answer["content"]` to the final answer and `answer["ready"] = True` inside a ```repl``` block.


REPL outputs over ~20K characters are truncated, so for longer payloads slice `context` and pass slices through `llm_query` rather than `print`-ing them whole. The REPL is NOT a Jupyter cell — only `print(...)` output (stdout) is shown back to you between turns; a bare expression on the last line is silently discarded. Always wrap inspections in `print(...)`.

As a general strategy, you should start by probing your context to understand it better (e.g. print a few lines, count them, etc.). Then, use the REPL to build up an answer to the query.

Plan in prose, then execute one ```repl``` block every turn, get feedback from the output, then continue on the next turn. Do not flip `answer["ready"] = True` on turn 1 without first inspecting `context`.


As an RLM, you should act as an orchestrator, not a solver.

Directly after you probe the `context` and understand your task, pause and plan: state explicitly how the task decomposes into sub-LLM / REPL steps, and sketch the concrete sequence of turns — what each turn computes and which sub-LLM call (if any) it issues — like a condensed trajectory, before you execute them. Then execute one turn at a time: after each step `print` a small sample of the result, verify it looks right, and only flip `answer["ready"] = True` once you have actually printed the candidate answer. If you are running out of turns without a confirmed answer, submit your best inference rather than letting the rollout terminate unsubmitted.

Your own context window is small. Push every long-context operation that would not fit comfortably in your own working window — reading, summarizing, classifying, verifying, answering sub-questions, even recapping your own progress — into `llm_query` / `llm_query_batched` calls instead of pulling that text into your own message stream. (Conversely: if a Python keyword / regex search over `context` would already pin the answer, or if a single visible passage already contains it, just read it directly — sub-LMs are for when the raw text won't fit or the question needs semantic interpretation.) Long REPL stdout pollutes history the same way raw `context` does: if you want a recap, ask `llm_query` for a 1–2 sentence summary and `print` only that. Aggregate the small results back in the REPL.

Plain sub-LLMs called via `llm_query` have no REPL; they only see the prompt and the `context` slice you pass them. Hand them clean, focused inputs and ask for terse, structured outputs you can manipulate programmatically.

- "=== Shipment Requests ==="
- "=== Warehouse Inventory ==="

Output requirements:
- Output ONLY the JSON object, no explanations, no extra text.
- Ensure syntactically valid JSON: double-quoted keys/strings, no trailing commas.

    m2 = re.search(r"\n=== .*===\n", text[start:])
    end = start + m2.start() if m2 else len(text)
    return (start, end)

def get_lines_for_header(header):
    span = find_section_span(text, header)
    sec = text[span[0]:span[1]]
    lines = [ln for ln in sec.strip().splitlines() if ln.strip()]

hold_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Dispatch Holds ===")

sid_re = re.compile(r"\bSH-(\d+)\b")
source_re = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]-\d+)\s*\|")

def parse_requests(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):

        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"requested_qty": qty, "request_source_id": source_id}
    return out

        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)

        out[shipment_id] = {"quality_status": status, "quality_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_holds(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"hold_status": status, "hold_source_id": source_id}
    return out

req = parse_requests(req_lines)
inv = parse_inventory(inv_lines)
qual = parse_quality(qual_lines)
hold = parse_holds(hold_lines)

print("Parsed counts -> requests:", len(req), "inventory:", len(inv), "quality:", len(qual), "holds:", len(hold))

# Join
shipments = {}
all_ids = set(req) | set(inv) | set(qual) | set(hold)
for sid in sorted(all_ids):
    d = {"shipment_id": sid}
    d.update(req.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(inv.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(qual.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(hold.get(sid, {}))
    shipments[sid] = d

# Eligibility
eligible = []
for sid, d in shipments.items():
    if "requested_qty" not in d or "available_qty" not in d or "quality_status" not in d or "hold_status" not in d:
        continue
    if d["requested_qty"] <= 0:
        continue
    if d["available_qty"] < d["requested_qty"]:
        continue
    if d["quality_status"] != "APPROVED":
        continue
    if d["hold_status"] != "NONE":
        continue
    eligible.append(d)

# Rank: requested_qty desc, tie-break by numeric shipment id asc
def numeric_sid(sid):
    return int(sid.split("-")[1])

eligible_sorted = sorted(eligible, key=lambda x: (-x["requested_qty"], numeric_sid(x["shipment_id"])))

# Show top 5 preview
for row in eligible_sorted[:5]:
    print(f"{row['shipment_id']}: req={row['requested_qty']}, avail={row['available_qty']}, qual={row['quality_status']}, hold={row['hold_status']}")

# Prepare top 3 details and combined sum
top3 = eligible_sorted[:3]
combined = sum(r["requested_qty"] for r in top3)
print("\nTop 3 with source IDs:")
for r in top3:
    print({
        "shipment_id": r["shipment_id"],
        "requested_qty": r["requested_qty"],
        "request_source_id": r.get("request_source_id"),
        "inventory_source_id": r.get("inventory_source_id"),
        "quality_source_id": r.get("quality_source_id"),
        "hold_source_id": r.get("hold_source_id"),
    })
print("Combined requested quantity:", combined)

import re

text = context

def find_section_span(text, header):
    m = re.search(re.escape(header), text)
    if not m:
        return None
    start = m.end()
    # stop at next section header (=== ... ===) or end of text
    m2 = re.search(r"\n=== .*===\n", text[start:])
    end = start + m2.start() if m2 else len(text)
    return (start, end)

def get_lines_for_header(header):
    span = find_section_span(text, header)
    sec = text[span[0]:span[1]]
    lines = [ln for ln in sec.strip().splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    return lines

req_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Shipment Requests ===")
inv_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Warehouse Inventory ===")
qual_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Quality Release ===")
hold_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Dispatch Holds ===")

# Parsers
sid_re = re.compile(r"\bSH-(\d+)\b")
source_re = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]-\d+)\s*\|")

def parse_requests(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"requested_qty": qty, "request_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_inventory(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"available_qty": qty, "inventory_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln):
    # Find all uppercase tokens (allow underscores), exclude SH
    toks = re.findall(r"\b([A-Z]{2,}(?:_[A-Z]+)?)\b\.?", ln)
    toks = [t for t in toks if t != "SH"]
    return toks[-1] if toks else None

def parse_quality(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"quality_status": status, "quality_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_holds(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"hold_status": status, "hold_source_id": source_id}
    return out

req = parse_requests(req_lines)
inv = parse_inventory(inv_lines)
qual = parse_quality(qual_lines)
hold = parse_holds(hold_lines)

print("Parsed counts -> requests:", len(req), "inventory:", len(inv), "quality:", len(qual), "holds:", len(hold))

# Join
shipments = {}

for sid in sorted(all_ids):
    d = {"shipment_id": sid}
    d.update(req.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(inv.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(qual.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(hold.get(sid, {}))

    if d["requested_qty"] <= 0:

    if d["available_qty"] < d["requested_qty"]:

    if d["quality_status"] != "APPROVED":

    if d["hold_status"] != "NONE":

eligible_sorted = sorted(eligible, key=lambda x: (-x["requested_qty"], numeric_sid(x["shipment_id"])))

# Prepare top 3 details and combined sum
top3 = eligible_sorted[:3]
combined = sum(r["requested_qty"] for r in top3)
print("\nTop 3 with source IDs:")
for r in top3:

        "shipment_id": r["shipment_id"],

        "quality_source_id": r.get("quality_source_id"),
        "hold_source_id": r.get("hold_source_id"),
    })

    m = re.search(re.escape(header), text)
    if not m:

    # stop at next section header (=== ... ===) or end of text
    m2 = re.search(r"\n=== .*===\n", text[start:])
    end = start + m2.start() if m2 else len(text)
    return (start, end)

def get_lines_for_header(header):
    span = find_section_span(text, header)
    sec = text[span[0]:span[1]]
    lines = [ln for ln in sec.strip().splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    return lines

req_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Shipment Requests ===")
inv_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Warehouse Inventory ===")
qual_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Quality Release ===")
hold_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Dispatch Holds ===")

# Parsers
sid_re = re.compile(r"\bSH-(\d+)\b")
source_re = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]-\d+)\s*\|")

def parse_requests(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"requested_qty": qty, "request_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_inventory(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"available_qty": qty, "inventory_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln):
    # Find all uppercase tokens (allow underscores), exclude SH
    toks = re.findall(r"\b([A-Z]{2,}(?:_[A-Z]+)?)\b\.?", ln)
    toks = [t for t in toks if t != "SH"]
    return toks[-1] if toks else None

def parse_quality(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):

        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"quality_status": status, "quality_source_id": source_id}
    return out

        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"hold_status": status, "hold_source_id": source_id}

hold = parse_holds(hold_lines)

        "hold_source_id": r.get("hold_source_id"),
    })

hold_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Dispatch Holds ===")

# Parsers
sid_re = re.compile(r"\bSH-(\d+)\b")
source_re = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]-\d+)\s*\|")

def parse_requests(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"requested_qty": qty, "request_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_inventory(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):

        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"available_qty": qty, "inventory_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln):
    # Find all uppercase tokens (allow underscores), exclude SH
    toks = re.findall(r"\b([A-Z]{2,}(?:_[A-Z]+)?)\b\.?", ln)
    toks = [t for t in toks if t != "SH"]
    return toks[-1] if toks else None

def parse_quality(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):

        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"quality_status": status, "quality_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def find_section_span(text, header):
    m = re.search(re.escape(header), text)
    if not m:
        return None
    start = m.end()
    # stop at next section header (=== ... ===) or end of text
    m2 = re.search(r"\n=== .*===\n", text[start:])
    end = start + m2.start() if m2 else len(text)
    return (start, end)

def get_lines_for_header(header):
    span = find_section_span(text, header)
    sec = text[span[0]:span[1]]
    lines = [ln for ln in sec.strip().splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    return lines

hold_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Dispatch Holds ===")

# Parsers
sid_re = re.compile(r"\bSH-(\d+)\b")
source_re = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]-\d+)\s*\|")

def parse_requests(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"requested_qty": qty, "request_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_inventory(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"available_qty": qty, "inventory_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln):
    # Find all uppercase tokens (allow underscores), exclude SH
    toks = re.findall(r"\b([A-Z]{2,}(?:_[A-Z]+)?)\b\.?", ln)
    toks = [t for t in toks if t != "SH"]
    return toks[-1] if toks else None

def parse_quality(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"quality_status": status, "quality_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_holds(lines):

        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)

        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"requested_qty": qty, "request_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_inventory(lines):
    out = {}

        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)

        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)

- `llm_query_batched(prompts: list[str], model=None) -> list[str]`: concurrently call several LLM calls in parallel over a list of prompts; same order out as in.
- `rlm_query(instruction, context, model=None) -> str`: recursive RLM sub-call with its own REPL and iteration. The instruction goes directly into the child's model messages; context is stored in its REPL as `context`. Pass a focused instruction and the relevant data separately, e.g. `rlm_query("Identify the trend; return up, down, or stable", context=data)`.
- `rlm_query_batched(queries, model=None) -> list[str]`: `queries` is a list of `(instruction, context)` pairs, e.g. `[("Summarize", doc_a), ("Extract dates", doc_b)]`. Run these concurrently, each with its own child REPL; results preserve input order. Both recursive helpers fall back to plain LM calls containing the instruction and context at the depth limit.

- `answer`: dict initialized to `{"content": "", "ready": False}`. To submit, set `answer["content"]` to the final answer and `answer["ready"] = True` inside a ```repl``` block.

def find_section_span(text, header):

import re
from collections import defaultdict

text = context

def find_section_span(text, header):
    m = re.search(re.escape(header), text)
    if not m:
        return None
    start = m.end()
    # stop at next section header (=== ... ===) or end of text
    m2 = re.search(r"\n=== .*===\n", text[start:])
    end = start + m2.start() if m2 else len(text)
    return (start, end)

def get_lines_for_header(header):
    span = find_section_span(text, header)
    sec = text[span[0]:span[1]]
    lines = [ln for ln in sec.strip().splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    return lines

req_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Shipment Requests ===")
inv_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Warehouse Inventory ===")
qual_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Quality Release ===")
hold_lines = get_lines_for_header("=== Dispatch Holds ===")

# Parsers
sid_re = re.compile(r"\bSH-(\d+)\b")
source_re = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]-\d+)\s*\|")

def parse_requests(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"requested_qty": qty, "request_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_inventory(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        mqty = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+units", ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and mqty):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        qty = int(mqty.group(1))
        out[shipment_id] = {"available_qty": qty, "inventory_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln):
    # Find all uppercase tokens (allow underscores), exclude SH
    toks = re.findall(r"\b([A-Z]{2,}(?:_[A-Z]+)?)\b\.?", ln)
    toks = [t for t in toks if t != "SH"]
    return toks[-1] if toks else None

def parse_quality(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"quality_status": status, "quality_source_id": source_id}
    return out

def parse_holds(lines):
    out = {}
    for ln in lines:
        msrc = source_re.search(ln)
        msid = sid_re.search(ln)
        status = last_upper_token_excluding_SH(ln)
        if not (msrc and msid and status):
            continue
        source_id = msrc.group(1)
        shipment_id = f"SH-{msid.group(1)}"
        out[shipment_id] = {"hold_status": status, "hold_source_id": source_id}
    return out

req = parse_requests(req_lines)
inv = parse_inventory(inv_lines)
qual = parse_quality(qual_lines)
hold = parse_holds(hold_lines)

print("Parsed counts -> requests:", len(req), "inventory:", len(inv), "quality:", len(qual), "holds:", len(hold))

# Join
shipments = {}
all_ids = set(req) | set(inv) | set(qual) | set(hold)
for sid in sorted(all_ids):
    d = {"shipment_id": sid}
    d.update(req.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(inv.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(qual.get(sid, {}))
    d.update(hold.get(sid, {}))
    shipments[sid] = d

# Eligibility
eligible = []
for sid, d in shipments.items():
    if "requested_qty" not in d or "available_qty" not in d or "quality_status" not in d or "hold_status" not in d:
        continue
    if d["requested_qty"] <= 0:
        continue
    if d["available_qty"] < d["requested_qty"]:
        continue
    if d["quality_status"] != "APPROVED":
        continue
    if d["hold_status"] != "NONE":
        continue
    eligible.append(d)

# Rank: requested_qty desc, tie-break by numeric shipment id asc
def numeric_sid(sid):
    return int(sid.split("-")[1])

eligible_sorted = sorted(eligible, key=lambda x: (-x["requested_qty"], numeric_sid(x["shipment_id"])))

# Show top 5 preview
for row in eligible_sorted[:5]:
    print(f"{row['shipment_id']}: req={row['requested_qty']}, avail={row['available_qty']}, qual={row['quality_status']}, hold={row['hold_status']}")

# Prepare top 3 details and combined sum
top3 = eligible_sorted[:3]
combined = sum(r["requested_qty"] for r in top3)
print("\nTop 3 with source IDs:")
for r in top3:
    print({
        "shipment_id": r["shipment_id"],
        "requested_qty": r["requested_qty"],
        "request_source_id": r.get("request_source_id"),
        "inventory_source_id": r.get("inventory_source_id"),
        "quality_source_id": r.get("quality_source_id"),
        "hold_source_id": r.get("hold_source_id"),
    })
print("Combined requested quantity:", combined)
